Tempo and beats, spectrum, pictures of the waveform and the spectrogram, and silence.

## audioBpm

Detect the tempo of audio and where its beats fall

```js
audioBpm( audio, minBpm=60, maxBpm=200 )
```

| Argument | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | any | required | The audio buffer. |
| `minBpm` | double | `60` | Lowest tempo to consider. Defaults to 60. |
| `maxBpm` | double | `200` | Highest tempo to consider. Defaults to 200. |

**Returns** A struct with bpm (0 if there is no clear pulse), confidence (0 to 1) and beats, the beat times in seconds.

## audioSpectrum

Get the level of audio in log spaced frequency bands, in dB

```js
audioSpectrum( audio, bands=16, minHz=40, maxHz=16000, start=0, seconds=0 )
```

| Argument | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | any | required | The audio buffer. |
| `bands` | integer | `16` | How many bands. Defaults to 16. |
| `minHz` | double | `40` | Lower edge of the first band. Defaults to 40. |
| `maxHz` | double | `16000` | Upper edge of the last band, capped at half the sample rate. Defaults to 16000. |
| `start` | double | `0` | Start in seconds. Defaults to 0. |
| `seconds` | double | `0` | Length to analyse in seconds, 0 for the rest. Defaults to 0. |

**Returns** An array of band levels in dB, lowest frequency first. -120 means nothing.

## audioSpectrogram

Get the band levels of audio over time, for drawing or analysis

```js
audioSpectrogram( audio, bands=16, frames=64, minHz=40, maxHz=16000 )
```

| Argument | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | any | required | The audio buffer. |
| `bands` | integer | `16` | How many bands. Defaults to 16. |
| `frames` | integer | `64` | How many time slices. Defaults to 64. |
| `minHz` | double | `40` | Lower edge of the first band. Defaults to 40. |
| `maxHz` | double | `16000` | Upper edge of the last band. Defaults to 16000. |

**Returns** An array of frames, each an array of band levels in dB.

## audioWaveformImage

Draws how loud a sound is over time, the way a player or an editor shows it. For each column of the picture the highest and lowest sample are drawn pale and the average level (RMS) solid, so a loud, steady sound and a sparse, peaky one look different. Silence is a thin line. The picture can go in a web page, a report or a podcast page.

```js
audioWaveformImage( audio, width=800, height=160, format="", path="", color="#3b82f6", background="", style="filled", split=false )
```

| Argument | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | any | required | The audio buffer. |
| `width` | integer | `800` | Pixels across, 8 to 8192. Defaults to 800. |
| `height` | integer | `160` | Pixels down, 8 to 4096. Defaults to 160. |
| `format` | string | `""` | svg or png. Left out, it follows the extension of path, and is svg when there is none. |
| `path` | string | `""` | A file to write the picture to. Folders are created and an existing file is replaced. |
| `color` | string | `"#3b82f6"` | The color of the waveform as a hex color, #rgb, #rrggbb or #rrggbbaa. Defaults to #3b82f6. |
| `background` | string | `""` | The color behind it as a hex color. Left out it is transparent. |
| `style` | string | `"filled"` | filled for a continuous shape, or bars for separate bars. Defaults to filled. |
| `split` | boolean | `false` | True to give each channel of a stereo sound its own lane. Defaults to false, which draws both over one another. |

**Returns** The absolute path of the file when path is given. Otherwise the SVG as a string, or the PNG as binary data.

## audioSpectrogramImage

Draws which frequencies are in a sound and when: time runs across, frequency up (low at the bottom, on a log scale like hearing) and loudness is the color. A steady tone is a horizontal line, a drum hit a vertical smear, speech a pattern of bands. The color scale is set by the loudest point of the picture, so quiet and loud recordings both fill the range.

```js
audioSpectrogramImage( audio, width=800, height=256, format="", path="", minHz=40, maxHz=16000, rangeDb=80, scale="magma" )
```

| Argument | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | any | required | The audio buffer. |
| `width` | integer | `800` | Pixels across, 8 to 4000. Each column is one slice of time. Defaults to 800. |
| `height` | integer | `256` | Pixels up, 8 to 512. Each row is one band of frequencies. Defaults to 256. |
| `format` | string | `""` | png or svg. Left out, it follows the extension of path, and is png when there is none. The SVG holds the PNG, since a spectrogram has a color for every point. |
| `path` | string | `""` | A file to write the picture to. Folders are created and an existing file is replaced. |
| `minHz` | double | `40` | The lowest frequency shown. Defaults to 40. |
| `maxHz` | double | `16000` | The highest frequency shown. Defaults to 16000. |
| `rangeDb` | double | `80` | How many dB below the loudest point still show, 10 to 120. Defaults to 80. |
| `scale` | string | `"magma"` | The colors, from quiet to loud: magma, viridis or gray. Defaults to magma. |

**Returns** The absolute path of the file when path is given. Otherwise the PNG as binary data, or the SVG as a string.

## audioFft

Get the frequency spectrum of one window of audio

```js
audioFft( audio, size=2048, start=0 )
```

| Argument | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | any | required | The audio buffer. |
| `size` | integer | `2048` | FFT size, a power of two. Defaults to 2048. |
| `start` | double | `0` | Where the window starts, in seconds. Defaults to 0. |

**Returns** A struct with frequencies (Hz) and magnitudes (1 for a full scale sine), arrays of size/2+1 values.

## audioDetectSilence

Find the silent stretches of audio

```js
audioDetectSilence( audio, thresholdDb=-50, minSeconds=0.3 )
```

| Argument | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | any | required | The audio buffer. |
| `thresholdDb` | double | `-50` | Level below which audio counts as silent, in dB. Defaults to -50. |
| `minSeconds` | double | `0.3` | The shortest silence to report. Defaults to 0.3. |

**Returns** An array of structs with start, end and duration in seconds.

## audioTrimSilence

Cut the silence off the start and the end of audio

```js
audioTrimSilence( audio, thresholdDb=-50, pad=0 )
```

| Argument | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | any | required | The audio buffer. |
| `thresholdDb` | double | `-50` | Level below which audio counts as silent, in dB. Defaults to -50. |
| `pad` | double | `0` | Seconds of silence to keep on each side. Defaults to 0. |

**Returns** A new audio buffer.
